support.text: Free, open-source software maintained by the WordPress contributor community. Community forums and commercial hosting/support are available. WordPress.org software is separate from the WordPress.com hosting service.

technology.text: PHP server application with MySQL or MariaDB; Apache or Nginx is recommended. Browser interface and generated pages use HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

capabilities.text: Themes and block editing; plugins; user roles; media management; custom content types; REST API for external applications.

limitations.text: Self-hosted installations require backups and ongoing core, theme, and plugin updates. Vulnerable or unmaintained plugins can expose the site to attacks; installing more plugins adds maintenance work.

examples.text: NASA — public news, science, and mission information.

support.text: Free, open-source software developed by a global community. The Drupal Association supports project infrastructure; community help and paid service providers are available.

technology.text: PHP with Symfony components and Twig templates; MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, or SQLite. Apache/Nginx serves the site; Composer manages dependencies. Browser pages use HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

capabilities.text: Structured content types and fields; modules and themes; multilingual publishing; permissions; APIs for delivering content to separate frontends.

limitations.text: Deployment must satisfy PHP, database, and Composer requirements. Windows production hosting is unsupported. Assessment: this dependency management makes self-hosting more involved than simply uploading static pages.

examples.text: Drupal.org — community documentation and project resources.

support.text: Free, open-source CMS developed by community volunteers. Open Source Matters, Inc. provides organizational support; community documentation and extension vendors offer help.

technology.text: PHP application using an MVC framework with MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL. Runs on Apache, Nginx, or IIS. Templates deliver HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to browsers.

capabilities.text: Templates and extensions; multilingual content; user access controls; article and media management; customizable layouts.

limitations.text: Extensions must be checked for compatibility before upgrades. Customized or older extensions can need developer assistance during migration, increasing the work required to keep a site current.

examples.text: Joomla.org — the project’s own CMS website.

support.text: Open-source publishing software run by the nonprofit Ghost Foundation. Ghost(Pro) offers paid managed hosting; self-hosted users can use community forums.

technology.text: JavaScript on Node.js with MySQL for supported production hosting, typically behind Nginx on Ubuntu. Handlebars themes produce browser-facing HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

capabilities.text: Visual publishing editor; custom themes; newsletters; free and paid memberships; integrations and APIs for custom frontends.

limitations.text: Official production support targets a narrow server stack. Clustering and sharding are unsupported. Self-hosting requires server maintenance and separate email delivery setup/services.

examples.text: 404 Media — independent technology journalism and subscriptions.

support.text: Free, open-source CMS created by Andy Miller and maintained by the Grav team and contributors. Community forums, documentation, and commercial services are available.

technology.text: PHP with Symfony components and Twig templates. Stores normal page content in Markdown files with YAML metadata instead of a SQL database. Themes render HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for browsers.

capabilities.text: Themes and plugins; Markdown editing; multilingual content; modular pages; caching; file-based backups and version control.

limitations.text: The normal page tree is awkward for large collections of structured records such as products or bookings. Those use cases need extra modeling with Flex types/plugins or custom development rather than ordinary pages.

examples.text: Grav documentation — the official learning and reference site, which identifies itself as powered by Grav.
